sources.title: 2025-2026 IFRC network country plan: Guinea
sources.organization: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, in support of the Red Cross Society of Guinea
sources.temporal_coverage: Reported 2024 flood events and response; 2025–2026 network plan
sources.methodology: Plan combines situational analysis and Red Cross operational reporting.
sources.limitations: No probability survey or independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Guinea: Selected Issues, IMF Country Report No. 24/131
sources.temporal_coverage: Hazard and coping-capacity context; macroeconomic adaptation simulations for 2024 onward
sources.methodology: IMF staff analysis of climate-risk indicators and DIGNAD macroeconomic scenario simulations.
sources.limitations: Comparative and modeled results are national macroeconomic analysis, not local household evidence.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Guinea
sources.temporal_coverage: Current vulnerability and institutional diagnostics; modeled climate, crop and urban-flood scenarios through 2050
sources.methodology: CCDR uses sector diagnostics, geospatial/climate modeling, and institutional/fragility review.
sources.limitations: Its macroeconomic model excludes resource tensions and climate-related outmigration.

claims.paraphrase: In 2024, flood waves in Siguiri, Kouroussa, Kankan, Mandiana and Gueckedou disrupted livelihoods and required humanitarian assistance.
claims.limitations: No prefecture-level affected totals or event attribution are provided.

claims.paraphrase: Floods account for over 75% of recorded natural hazards; the plan reports over 70,000 affected and needing aid in the prior five years.
The plan links coastal sea-level rise to salinization, flooding, water shortages, crop and infrastructure damage; floods also affect northern Guinea.
claims.limitations: The plan describes broad zones, not mapped communities or local exposure rates.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, Red Cross Society of Guinea profile
claims.paraphrase: The Red Cross Society of Guinea operates 38 prefectural/communal and 303 sub-prefectural committees covering disaster response, climate action, early warning and migration assistance.
claims.limitations: Network size and described functions do not establish coverage quality or effectiveness.

claims.paraphrase: An August 2024 DREF allocation of CHF 467,835 supported Guinea Red Cross aid for 13,300 flood-affected people in Kankan region over four months, including cash, health, WASH and protection/accountability services.
claims.limitations: The plan reports delivered activity, not independently evaluated recovery outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: IMF reports Guinea among 20 countries with the lowest climate-risk coping capacity on institutional and infrastructure factors, likely reflecting long-standing constraints and weak connectivity.
claims.limitations: This is a comparative national indicator, not a prefecture or household measure; the explanation is qualified.

claims.paraphrase: IMF DIGNAD simulations find grant-financed resilient infrastructure plus improved public-investment efficiency yields the smallest modeled disaster-related GDP loss and debt increase.
claims.scenario: Scenario 3 invests an additional 1% of GDP in resilient infrastructure during 2024–2028 using grants, raises public investment efficiency from 50% to 70%, and models a hypothetical 1%-of-GDP disaster in 2029.
claims.limitations: This is a modeled macroeconomic result, not observed investment or measured local resilience.

claims.paraphrase: CCDR says northern degradation/desertification threatens pastoral and farming communities, heightening intercommunal tensions; insecure tenure compounds rural poverty and gender inequality.
claims.limitations: Fragility appendix is contextual, not event-level causal evidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report explicitly links northern degradation/desertification to intercommunal tensions (PDF p. 110).

claims.locator: PDF p. 106, Annex 2, climate readiness assessment
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR says education-adaptation strategies are underimplemented due to political instability and high costs; a 2013 health-adaptation plan was not implemented for lack of funds.
claims.limitations: These are reported plan-implementation gaps, without subnational delivery measures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report identifies political instability as a barrier to education-adaptation implementation (PDF p. 106).

claims.paraphrase: For 2050 under SSP3-7.0, modeled annual urban flood damages rise without adaptation in Conakry, Nzérékoré, Kankan, Kindia, Siguiri and Kamsar; adaptation reduces increases in four cities and turns Conakry and Kamsar negative.
claims.scenario: 2050, SSP3-7.0; percent change in expected urban flood damages relative to historical conditions, with and without modeled adaptation.
claims.limitations: These are modeled city-scale outputs, not observed losses, household exposure or adaptation actually delivered.

access_audit.notes: Opened the 16-page plan and read the country risk, climate, named flood and Siguiri response passages.
Opened and inspected the IMF climate-risk coping-capacity assessment and DIGNAD adaptation scenarios.
Opened the 115-page public CCDR; inspected future flood scenarios, adaptation implementation gaps and the fragility appendix.
access_audit.reuse_terms: The report allows noncommercial reproduction with attribution; commercial use is restricted.

search_audit.query: Guinea climate vulnerability subnational prefecture report drought flood adaptation PDF government UN
search_audit.outcome: Opened the 2025 CCDR and IFRC plan. They add named urban flood scenarios, regional vulnerability context and 2024 flood records for five prefectures; the 2026 NAP PDF was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Guinea climate natural-resource conflict pastoral land water report prefecture Guinea
search_audit.outcome: The full CCDR appendix links northern degradation/desertification to intercommunal tensions. A UNOWAS pastoralism study surfaced, but its PDF returned 403 and indexed text was excluded.

search_audit.query: Guinea climate adaptation conflict insecurity disrupted aid access local report Guinea
search_audit.outcome: The CCDR reports political instability and cost impeded education-adaptation implementation. No inspected source documented acute conflict or insecurity interrupting climate-service or aid delivery; this is not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: Guinea community disaster risk resilience capacity adaptation local early warning assessment report PDF
search_audit.outcome: IFRC reports the Red Cross committee network and 2024 Kankan-region flood response; IMF analyzes national adaptation scenarios. Neither report independently evaluates local resilience outcomes.

gaps: The official 2026 National Adaptation Plan record was accessible, but its linked PDF returned an internal retrieval error; no claims were drawn from metadata or search-indexed text.
The WFP Climate Response Analysis page provided only an abstract; its PDF link returned an HTML/error response, so the analysis was not used.
A UNOWAS study surfaced local farmer-pastoralist and water-competition material for Beyla and Boké/Boffa, but the original PDF returned HTTP 403; indexed excerpts were excluded.

The CCDR supplies contextual climate-fragility links and reported adaptation-implementation barriers, but the inspected sources do not establish event-level causal effects or document acute conflict disrupting aid delivery or climate services.
